newsitem.title: USA: Brazil coffee belt to turn cooler, no frost threat.
newsitem.headline: Brazil coffee belt to turn cooler, no frost threat.

text.p: Cooler temperatures are heading toward Brazil's coffee-growing regions next week, but there is no threat of frost, Weather Services Corp forecast Friday.
The first cool airmass of the Fall season moved into Argentina, causing traders in New York to take notice.
But while the weather will be unusally cool for this time of year, temperatures in Brazil's coffee-growing regions are only expected to drop into the low 50s Fahrenheit (low teens C), WSC said.

"There is no threat," said WSC meteorogist Mike Palmerino. "Normal temperatures in the coffee belt this time of year are in the low 60s F, so it's a surprise to see them fall into the low 50s. But you need temperatures in the mid-30s to get frost and they are not going to get even close to that."
Palmerino noted that there has never been a frost event this early in the season and stressed there was no correlation between unusally cool Fall weather and the likelyhood of a severe Winter.
Typically, the Brazil frost season begins in late May, but the most critical time for coffee plantations are mid-June to mid-August.

Two severe frosts in 1994, one in late June and another in early July, reduced Brazil's 1995/96 crop by some 50 percent and sent futures prices to near 10-year highs. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk 212 859 1640))
